I can’t run background checks or send you messages after this reply. I don’t have any automation, web, or messaging capability from here, and I can’t continue working in the background. I can, however, help you set up a reliable automatic monitor you can run (or a third‑party service) that will check every 5 minutes and notify you when the Acme status page recovers.

Below are practical options and ready-to-run examples. Tell me which notification channel you want (email, SMS, Slack, Teams, webhook, etc.) and whether you prefer a hosted service or a self-hosted script, and I’ll tailor instructions or the script for you.

1) Quick hosted monitoring (recommended if you want an easy setup)
- Use a monitoring service such as UptimeRobot, Pingdom, StatusCake, or similar.
- Steps (typical):
  - Sign up for the service.
  - Add a new HTTP(S) monitor pointing to the Acme status page URL.
  - Set the polling interval to 5 minutes.
  - Add alert contact(s): email, SMS, Slack webhook, or webhook URL.
- I can draft the exact settings and alert message text you should paste.

2) Self-hosted script + cron (you run this on a machine that’s always on)
- Basic bash script that checks HTTP status, remembers previous state, and notifies on recovery.
- Fill in STATUS_URL and one notification method (email or Slack webhook). Save as /usr/local/bin/check_acme.sh and make executable (chmod +x).

Example (bash):
#!/bin/bash
STATUS_URL="https://status.acme.example"   # <--- set real URL
STATE_FILE="/tmp/acme_status_prev"
SLACK_WEBHOOK=""                            # <--- or leave empty if using email
ALERT_EMAIL="you@example.com"               # <--- set if using email

http_code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$STATUS_URL")
if [ "$http_code" -ge 200 ] && [ "$http_code" -lt 400 ]; then
  healthy=1
else
  healthy=0
fi

prev=$(cat "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)

if [ "$healthy" -eq 1 ] && [ "$prev" -eq 0 ]; then
  msg="Acme status recovered at $(date). Page: $STATUS_URL"
  if [ -n "$SLACK_WEBHOOK" ]; then
    curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' --data "{\"text\":\"$msg\"}" "$SLACK_WEBHOOK" >/dev/null 2>&1
  else
    echo "$msg" | mail -s "Acme status recovered" "$ALERT_EMAIL"
  fi
fi

echo "$healthy" > "$STATE_FILE"

- Cron entry to run every 5 minutes:
*/5 * * * * /usr/local/bin/check_acme.sh

3) Python script (if you prefer)
- I can provide a Python script that uses requests and smtplib (or Twilio) to poll and notify. Good if you want more complex checks (page content, availability of particular text).

4) More advanced: container + systemd timer or cloud lambda
- If you want reliability, run the script in a small VPS, container, or use a serverless function with scheduled trigger. I can provide step-by-step for any of those.

5) Alert message template
- If you want the exact notification text to send when recovery occurs, here’s a concise template you can use:
"Acme status page recovered at [timestamp]. URL: [status page]. Please verify services."

Next step from me
- Tell me:
  - Which notification channel do you want (email, SMS, Slack, Teams, webhook)?
  - Do you want a hosted service (UptimeRobot/Pingdom) or a self-hosted script?
  - If self-hosted, do you want the bash script or Python version, and the OS where it will run?
I’ll send the tailored script/config and instructions (including any credentials placeholders and exact cron/systemd entries).
